brief: Deutsche Bank's daily macro note reports a stagflation-driven cross-asset selloff and traces it to one chain. No end is in sight to the US-Iran conflict and investors now expect a longer Strait of Hormuz closure, reinforced by Houthi rebels capturing Mokha near Bab el-Mandeb and Saudi output at its lowest since 1990, so Brent rose 6.34% to $107.63/bbl and the whole futures curve moved higher. Higher energy prices fuelled expectations of faster rate hikes. The ECB hiked 25bp to 2.50% with hawkish elements, a new line that inflation stays well above target and a 2028 core forecast raised to 2.3%, leaving markets pricing three more hikes, though DB's European economists still see only one, in December, to 2.75%. Stronger PCE-relevant PPI components lifted September Fed hike odds from 60% to 72%. Yields rose across the board, Germany's 2yr up 16.6bps and the 10yr Treasury to 4.96%, with a $5.19bn Treasury buyback falling short of the $6bn maximum. Equities fell a fourth session and Asia extended the move overnight. Today's US CPI is the last big release before the Fed, with DB at 0.38% headline and 0.21% core.
